properties.name: The served working instructions never name the tool that answers "does this already exist", and one consumer rebuilt four things that did
properties.source: flo2 reflow2_feedback.md, 2026-09-19 addendum (F24, F25 and the meta-point)
properties.statement:
FLO2'S META-POINT, and the reporter calls it the most useful thing in their addendum. FOUR TIMES flo2 has built something reflow2 already served — skill `audience`, skill `summary`, the subject/record split on loop findings, and now the ingest and topic tools. Every time the conclusion filed upstream was 'reflow2 should add X', and every time X existed.

MEASURED 2026-09-20: the served working instructions (getting-started/AGENTS.md, the document `get_instructions` returns, 416 lines) mention `get_skill` and `list_skills` twice between them and name `find_tools` ZERO TIMES. The instructions describe the loop and name the constructors; nothing in them tells a reader that the surface can be ASKED whether a thing exists.

⭐ SO THE RESIDUE IS NOT CAPABILITY, IT IS REFLEX — their word, and the evidence is in the same addendum: BOTH of its discoveries came from two `find_tools` calls phrased as jobs ('compose a prompt for a model that turns what a person said into design entries', 'the slice of the design relevant to this sentence'). The catalogue worked exactly as designed the moment it was reached for. What is missing is anything that prompts reaching for it BEFORE building.

THEIR PROPOSED LINE, costing one sentence: 'before you build a capability against reflow2, search for it: find_tools takes a job description.' They observe it would have saved four reinventions, and would have saved their own session writing two of the entries triaged earlier tonight against a surface that had already answered part of them.

⚠️ NOTE WHAT THIS IS NOT. It is not the discoverability of the tools, which is measured and ratcheted; every tool ranks for a job sentence and the corpus proves it. It is that the one document every session receives unasked does not say the catalogue is there.

PRIOR ART FOUND ON A SECOND PASS, 2026-09-20, by running the search step the first pass skipped — which is itself an instance of the thing being reported.

⭐ ANTHONY ASKED FOR THIS ON 2026-08-11, IN HIS OWN WORDS, and it is recorded as dec:idea-search-first-fires-without-being-remembered: 'we need to make the search the graph first a requirement that is automatic.' That idea measured the same shape and reached the same conclusion — the rule is already written into FIVE served skills and still depends on somebody loading one, so the ask is not for the rule, it is for the TRIGGER. It also names the general mechanism, req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue (PROPOSED, unbuilt): a discipline that applies mid-task is delivered at the TOOL that triggers it, not from a catalogue read once at handshake.

⚠️ THEY ARE NOT THE SAME ASK AND BOTH ARE TRUE. The 2026-08-11 idea is SEARCH THE GRAPH before adding a node, to avoid near-duplicate nodes. flo2's is SEARCH THE TOOL SURFACE before building a capability, to avoid reinventing something served. Different catalogue, different reader, same missing trigger — and the second has a measurement the first did not: four things rebuilt, each filed upstream as a missing feature.

📌 AND THE HONEST NOTE ABOUT THIS RECORD: the first pass of this triage measured the instructions and formed a cause without searching for what the design already said, so it missed an idea in the owner's own words and an accepted requirement that is the mechanism for both. That is exactly the failure the triage skill's step 2 exists to prevent, and it cost one pass.
